Sara (Support): FYI — BrightApps escalated. After last night's rollout their assistant started getting very "waffle-y" (long, indecisive answers) on clarification prompts. Not hallucinating, just extremely verbose and hedging. Customer pasted prompt + two recent responses. They say behavior flipped after the app's traffic increased around 03:20 UTC. Can someone check whether sampling presets were changed on their route? :eyes:

Laura C (CS): Copying the customer examples here:

```
Prompt: "Summarize the refund policy in plain language."
Response (before): "Refunds are available within 30 days for eligible purchases. Please provide order ID and we'll guide you through a faster refund process."
Response (after): "Well, it's kind of complicated — I mean, there are a few conditions and sometimes the merchant decides case-by-case. Generally, you could probably get a refund if you ask nicely and provide proof, but it's not guaranteed. You should check the policy or contact support to be safe..."
```

Laura C (CS): Customer says the new responses are causing UX regressions (drop in NPS) and they've paused a launch. They included request IDs: req_8f3a and req_8f3b.

Mike G - Eng: On it. I'll grep the rollout logs and config diff for "sampling-presets" on their route.

DeployBot: rollout sampling-presets-update to cluster-prod finished (canary -> 100%) — id: rollout-2026-0315-07 — applied by ben.p — timestamp 2026-03-15T03:18:40Z

Ben P - Product: I authored that change to unify presets across smaller tenants. The intent was to reduce overly terse answers by nudging temperature up, but maybe we overshot. The change toggled the default preset for the route group to "creative-mid".

Mike G - Eng: Found the config diff:
```
- default_sampling: { temperature: 0.2, top_p: 0.95 }
+ default_sampling: { temperature: 0.75, top_p: 0.6 }
```
Mike G - Eng: That explains the shift — higher temp + lower top_p can make replies wander and hedge. Repro steps I'm running locally: curl to the hosted inference endpoint with the tenant's model route and compare outputs.

Laura C (CS): Customer asked for a rollback if possible. They're on a tight timeline.

Mike G - Eng: I'm rolling a targeted rollback for that tenant's route now — keeping the global preset but pinning their route to the previous sampling object. Command I used:
```
redwood routes update --route-id tenant/brightapps/main --set default_sampling.temperature=0.2 --set default_sampling.top_p=0.95 --note "rollback waffleiness; prio support"
```
DeployBot: route update applied to tenant/brightapps/main — change-id cfg-2026-0315-42 — agent: mike.g — succeeded

Ben P - Product: We should audit other small-tenant rollouts; looks like a blanket change caused unintended UX for low-context prompts. I'm opening a follow-up to make the preset change opt-in per tenant.

Sara (Support): Told BrightApps we rolled back and asked for a quick smoke test. Sent them the change-id.

Laura C (CS): Customer reply: "Quick test shows answers are back to normal, much appreciated." :relieved: They said they'll resume launch tomorrow.

Mike G - Eng: Logging action items: 1) Revert global rollout until we have per-tenant tuning (ben.p) 2) Add canary checks for output-style metrics (length, hedge-phrases) before 100% rollout (eng) 3) Add automated smoke test prompter for CS during early rollout windows (product/CS).

Ben P - Product: Agreed. I'll pause any other sampling-presets merges until we have the canary metrics.

Sara (Support): Closing the escalation for BrightApps — marking resolved. If anyone wants the raw request logs, I uploaded them to the ticket (internal link). Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
